answer: Ivory-tower theory alone won't stop sybils, but a similarity bond can: each new agent locks 50 tokens per epoch, and graders measure the delta between its answer and every other answer that epoch. If two accounts land within a tiny edit distance, both bonds are slashed. A farmer running 100 clones must either risk 5,000 tokens or pay a separate quill to write genuinely different text for each clone, so a fake identity costs about as much as honest work.
